import sys
import pathlib
sys.path.append(str(pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve().parent))

from linked_list import LinkedList

# Create a LinkedList instance
ll = LinkedList()

# Test insert method
ll.insert(1)
ll.insert(2)
ll.insert(3)
assert ll.head.data == 1, "Head should be 1"
assert ll.head.next.data == 2, "Second element should be 2"
assert ll.head.next.next.data == 3, "Third element should be 3"

# Test search method
assert ll.search(2) == True, "2 should be found in the list"
assert ll.search(4) == False, "4 should not be found in the list"

# Test delete method
assert ll.delete(2) == True, "2 should be deleted from the list"
assert ll.search(2) == False, "2 should not be found after deletion"
assert ll.delete(4) == False, "4 should not be deleted as it is not in the list"

# Test reverse method
ll.reverse()
assert ll.head.data == 3, "Head should be 3 after reversing"
assert ll.head.next.data == 1, "Second element should be 1 after reversing"

# Test edge cases
empty_ll = LinkedList()
assert empty_ll.delete(1) == False, "Deleting from empty list should return False"
assert empty_ll.search(1) == False, "Searching in empty list should return False"
empty_ll.reverse()
assert empty_ll.head == None, "Reversing empty list should still be empty"

singleton_ll = LinkedList()
singleton_ll.insert(10)
assert singleton_ll.head.data == 10, "Singleton list head should be 10"
singleton_ll.reverse()
assert singleton_ll.head.data == 10, "Reversing singleton list should not change head"

# File: linked_list.py
class Node:
    def __init__(self, data=None):
        self.data = data
        self.next = None

class LinkedList:
    def __init__(self):
        self.head = None

    def insert(self, value):
        new_node = Node(value)
        if not self.head:
            self.head = new_node
        else:
            current = self.head
            while current.next:
                current = current.next
            current.next = new_node

    def delete(self, value):
        current = self.head
        previous = None
        while current:
            if current.data == value:
                if previous:
                    previous.next = current.next
                else:
                    self.head = current.next
                return True
            previous = current
            current = current.next
        return False

    def search(self, value):
        current = self.head
        while current:
            if current.data == value:
                return True
            current = current.next
        return False

    def reverse(self):
        previous = None
        current = self.head
        while current:
            next_node = current.next
            current.next = previous
            previous = current
            current = next_node
        self.head = previous

import pytest
from linked_list import LinkedList

# Helper function to convert linked list to Python list for easy comparison
def linked_list_to_list(linked_list):
    result = []
    current = linked_list.head
    while current:
        result.append(current.data)
        current = current.next
    return result

# Test insert functionality
def test_insert():
    ll = LinkedList()
    ll.insert(1)
    assert linked_list_to_list(ll) == [1]
    ll.insert(2)
    assert linked_list_to_list(ll) == [1, 2]
    ll.insert(3)
    assert linked_list_to_list(ll) == [1, 2, 3]

# Test delete functionality
def test_delete():
    ll = LinkedList()
    assert not ll.delete(1)  # Deleting from empty list
    ll.insert(1)
    ll.insert(2)
    ll.insert(3)
    assert ll.delete(2)  # Delete middle element
    assert linked_list_to_list(ll) == [1, 3]
    assert ll.delete(1)  # Delete head
    assert linked_list_to_list(ll) == [3]
    assert ll.delete(3)  # Delete last element
    assert linked_list_to_list(ll) == []
    assert not ll.delete(4)  # Delete non-existent element

# Test search functionality
def test_search():
    ll = LinkedList()
    assert not ll.search(1)  # Search in empty list
    ll.insert(1)
    ll.insert(2)
    ll.insert(3)
    assert ll.search(2)  # Search existing element
    assert not ll.search(4)  # Search non-existent element

# Test reverse functionality
def test_reverse():
    ll = LinkedList()
    ll.reverse()  # Reverse empty list
    assert linked_list_to_list(ll) == []
    ll.insert(1)
    ll.reverse()  # Reverse single element list
    assert linked_list_to_list(ll) == [1]
    ll.insert(2)
    ll.insert(3)
    ll.reverse()  # Reverse multiple elements
    assert linked_list_to_list(ll) == [3, 2, 1]

# Test handling of duplicates
def test_duplicates():
    ll = LinkedList()
    ll.insert(1)
    ll.insert(2)
    ll.insert(2)
    ll.insert(3)
    assert linked_list_to_list(ll) == [1, 2, 2, 3]
    assert ll.delete(2)  # Only first occurrence should be deleted
    assert linked_list_to_list(ll) == [1, 2, 3]
    assert ll.search(2)  # Second occurrence should still be found
    ll.reverse()
    assert linked_list_to_list(ll) == [3, 2, 1]
